record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: What are the explicit correction terms, beyond the leading linear-in-temperature contribution, to the low-temperature specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot model in an interacting Luttinger-liquid environment, and do their exponents indeed match the exponents inferred earlier from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation?

evidence.quote: The corrections are still to be calculated but the exponents are expected to agree with those found earlier.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a side-coupled quantum-dot model defined as follows. A one-dimensional interacting electron system in the Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid universality class, characterized by a Luttinger parameter K (with K=1 being the noninteracting point and K≠1 corresponding to repulsive or attractive electron–electron interactions), is coupled by a tunneling amplitude t to a single localized level (the quantum dot) of energy ε_d, where the dot is attached at a single point of the lead but does not interrupt the lead (side-coupled geometry). Let the partition function and free energy F(T) be defined for this Hamiltonian at temperature T, and let the specific heat per unit length of the lead, with the bulk Luttinger-liquid contribution subtracted, be denoted C_d(T) = -T ∂²F_d/∂T², where F_d is the impurity contribution to the free energy.

It is known that, in the low-temperature regime T → 0, C_d(T) admits an asymptotic expansion whose leading term is linear in T, i.e. C_d(T) ≃ γ T + (subleading corrections). A renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation n_d(T) at low temperatures yields a set of anomalous power-law exponents {α_i(K)} (functions of the Luttinger parameter K) that govern the subleading temperature dependence of n_d(T) about its zero-temperature value.

Determine explicitly the subleading correction terms to C_d(T) beyond the leading γT contribution as T → 0, expressing them as a sum of power-law terms T^{β_j(K)} with explicit coefficients depending on K, t, and ε_d. In particular, decide whether the set of exponents {β_j(K)} appearing in the specific heat coincides with the set of exponents {α_i(K)} obtained from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation.
artifact.category_tag: Luttinger liquids and quantum impurity models
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published work explicitly computing the subleading low-temperature corrections to the specific heat of the side-coupled quantum-dot model in an interacting Luttinger liquid and matching their exponents against those obtained from the RG analysis of the dot occupation. Existing literature on related models (embedded dots, Kondo impurities in Luttinger liquids) discusses the leading Fermi-liquid–like linear-in-T behavior and notes anomalous power-law subleading exponents controlled by the Luttinger parameter K, but does not appear to provide the explicit calculation requested. The status therefore appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Quantum dot at a Luttinger liquid edge
status_evidence.snippet: Bethe Ansatz solutions for side-coupled and embedded quantum dot geometries in a Luttinger liquid, displaying non-Fermi-liquid exponents in specific heat and capacitance.
status_evidence.claim: Related Bethe-Ansatz work establishes existence of anomalous K-dependent exponents in dot thermodynamics but does not give explicit subleading specific-heat corrections matched to the dot-occupation RG exponents.

status_evidence.title: Underscreened Kondo impurities in a Luttinger liquid
status_evidence.snippet: Leading temperature dependence of thermodynamical quantities is Fermi-liquid-like, with anomalous power-law exponents in subleading corrections.
status_evidence.claim: In closely related impurity-in-Luttinger-liquid problems the leading specific heat is linear in T with anomalous subleading exponents, but explicit corrections for the side-coupled dot are not given.
